You buy the ticket, you take the ride. And what a deeply unsettling ride it is. We've unpacked the opportunistic tyrants, the tragic scapegoats, the silently complicit,
the unlikely heroes, the suffocating environment, and the indifferent cosmic horror. All in one town.
We walk through life assuming that barriers are built to protect us from the horrors outside. We build walls. We lock our doors.
We seek security in isolation, believing that the danger is always external. But the dome wasn't built to keep anything out. It was a terrarium designed to trap the poison inside, forcing the rot
to consume itself. The scariest thing about Chester's Mill isn't that they were trapped under the dome.
It's that sooner or later, every single one of us realizes we are already living in a closed system. We are all under the dome.
